items.label: Iran/Hormuz conflict escalating further -- new Houthi-Saudi front opened, no ceasefire
items.detail: Continued, widening escalation (live web search, Sept 8-9 sources): CENTCOM said US forces destroyed 5 Iranian crude tankers on Sept 8 (4 in the Gulf of Oman, 1 near Kharg Island) after the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US Navy warship for the second time in two days (evaded, no Americans harmed, per ABC News/CENTCOM). Separately, Iran-backed Houthis opened a new front on Sept 8, striking Saudi Arabian oil facilities -- Jazan City's industrial hub, Aramco facilities in Najran/Abha, and King Khalid Air Base -- wounding 73 people and briefly halting operations (per NPR/NBC News, Sept 8); the Saudi coalition called it a 'serious escalation' and vowed retaliation. Brent crude spiked to $99.16/bbl (+2.2%) and WTI to $94.46 (+3.3%) on Sept 8 on the Saudi-attack news, with a separate Sept 9 read putting Brent at $98.59. US equities fell in sympathy Sept 8 (S&P 500 -0.15%, Dow -0.58%/>600pts, Nasdaq -0.32%, per Yahoo Finance/CNBC). The account holds no direct oil & gas exposure but remains 69.28% concentrated in SPY5+SPYL, which would be hit hard by any broad equity selloff or oil-driven inflation surprise, and the account's Canadian mining names (CCJ, KGC) add a second channel of exposure if the conflict pressures global risk sentiment further.
items.recommendation: Do not add to SPY5/SPYL or initiate new discretionary equity purchases while the Iran/Hormuz conflict and the new Houthi-Saudi front remain unresolved and unretaliated-against. Prioritize the DBC diversification action above (the one true negative-correlation hedge found this run) over the lower-conviction EFA/DBC picks for the other two clusters, since DBC would benefit most directly from continued oil/inflation-driven stress.

items.label: US-Canada trade war escalating -- new risk channel for CCJ/KGC (Canadian miners)
items.detail: New this run (live web search, Sept 8 sources): Canada's retaliatory tariffs (15-50%) on 700+ US products took effect Sept 8, matching roughly $20B against existing US 50% tariffs on Canadian goods; Trump threatened a Bombardier aircraft sales ban and hiking auto tariffs to 50% starting January (per Bloomberg/ABC News, Sept 8). The account holds two Canadian-headquartered miners, CCJ (Cameco, $10,250.00, 2.09% of NAV) and KGC (Kinross Gold, $8,296.75, 1.69% of NAV), combined $18,546.75 = 3.78% of NAV -- a genuine, if secondary, exposure channel to cross-border trade friction on top of the commodity-price risk already flagged in the materials-satellites item above.
items.recommendation: No action needed at the current 3.78%-of-NAV combined exposure, but do not add to CCJ or KGC while the tariff dispute is actively escalating; watch for any Canada-specific export restrictions on uranium or gold (neither targeted so far per this run's search) before the next review.
